stories.headline: [The Economic Times] One in six Indian Schengen visa applications were rejected in 2025 - these countries denied the most
stories.summary: In 2025, one in six Indian Schengen visa applications were rejected. Slovenia had the highest rejection rate at 46.1%, while Germany and Switzerland had lower rates. Over 181,000 Schengen visa applications were filed by Indians, with Switzerland emerging as the most sought-after destination. France rejected more than 31,000 Indian visa applications, and other countries like Germany, Spain, the Netherlands, Estonia, and Malta also had significant rejection numbers. In contrast, Germany had the lowest rejection rate for Indian applicants. The rejection rates varied across Schengen countries, with some being more accessible to Indian travelers than others. The Schengen states received 11.7 million visa applications in 2024, indicating a high volume of interest in traveling to European countries.

stories.headline: [CNN] Trump’s doctor recommends he lose weight and exercise more but says he is in ‘excellent health’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's physician has reported that he is in "excellent health" following a routine medical examination at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center. However, the doctor has recommended that Trump lose weight and increase physical activity. According to the physician's memo, Trump currently weighs 238 pounds, up from 224 pounds at his last year's exam. The White House released the results of Trump's May physical, noting that his doctor has advised him to follow dietary measures to improve his overall health. At 79 years old, Trump's physician has emphasized the importance of weight loss and exercise to maintain his health. The report was released late Friday evening, providing an update on the President's health status. Trump's doctor has encouraged him to make lifestyle changes to support his overall well-being.

stories.headline: [ynetnews] The Greek minister who promoted an antisemitic book and became Europe’s loudest
stories.summary: Adonis Georgiadis, Greece's health minister, has a complex past regarding antisemitism. He previously promoted an antisemitic book, for which he later apologized to the Jewish community. Despite this, Georgiadis has become a vocal supporter of Zionism, earning him the title of Europe's loudest Zionist. His transformation has drawn attention, with some highlighting the contradiction between his past actions and current stance. Georgiadis' history has been scrutinized, particularly in the context of rising antisemitism in Europe. His apology and subsequent support for Zionism have sparked discussions about the importance of combating hatred and antisemitism. Georgiadis' case serves as a notable example of a public figure's evolution on sensitive issues.

stories.headline: [Samoa Observer] Spending sprees and political paranoia: A recipe for
stories.summary: Samoa faces a potential government shutdown by October if a budget is not passed, due to a law prohibiting further spending. The country's economy has sufficient funds, but the lack of a budget would trigger the shutdown. Meanwhile, the government has been criticized for spending sprees and exhibiting political paranoia. The Samoa Observer and several reporters remain barred from government press conferences, highlighting the tense relationship between the government and the media. The situation has been described as a "recipe for destruction," with concerns about the impact on the country's stability and economy. The government's actions have raised concerns among citizens and observers, who are calling for a more responsible and transparent approach to governance.

stories.headline: Snapdragon C debuts with 6nm, 1+3+4 CPU and on-device AI Gizmochina reports that Qualcomm unveiled the **Snapdragon C** platform ahead of Computex 2026 aimed at entry-level Arm Windows laptops starting near **$300**.
stories.summary: Qualcomm has unveiled the Snapdragon C platform, a new chip designed for entry-level Arm Windows laptops priced around $300. The Snapdragon C is built on a 6nm process and features an eight-core CPU in a 1+3+4 layout. It is paired with an Adreno GPU clocked at 900MHz and supports LPDDR5 memory. The platform is aimed at providing responsive performance, cool and quiet designs, and all-day battery life in budget laptops. The announcement was made ahead of Computex 2026, with the goal of powering laptops that can compete in the $300 price range. The Snapdragon C also includes on-device AI capabilities, enhancing the overall user experience in entry-level devices.

stories.headline: Honor Win Turbo unveiled with 10,000 mAh battery and durable chassis It's not a high-performance phone, but a high-endurance one.
stories.summary: Honor has unveiled the Win Turbo, a smartphone focused on endurance rather than high performance. The device features a large 10,000 mAh battery, allowing for up to 14.2 hours of gaming on a single charge. Despite its substantial battery, the Win Turbo has a slim design, measuring 7.98mm in thickness. The phone is part of Honor's Win series, which already includes the regular Win and Win RT, both equipped with active cooling fans and 10,000 mAh batteries. The Win Turbo boasts a premium metal middle frame, a 50MP OIS large horizontal camera module, and supports up to 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage. Its durable chassis and long-lasting battery make it an attractive option for users prioritizing endurance over raw performance.

stories.headline: 40 Xiaomi devices have now received the HyperOS 3.1 update Xiaomi HyperOS 3.1 is now available on 40 Xiaomi, Redmi, and Poco devices, bringing smoother performance, UI refinements, and new features.
stories.summary: Xiaomi's HyperOS 3.1 update is now available on 40 devices, including Xiaomi, Redmi, and Poco smartphones and tablets. The update brings improved performance, UI refinements, and new features to these devices. This rollout is part of Xiaomi's ongoing software update expansion, which started with a limited release on 8 devices in January 2026. Since then, the update has been made available to more devices, with the latest expansion including the POCO F6 in the global May update. The HyperOS 3.1 update is based on Android, with previous testing phases announced for Android 15 and Android 16. The update includes new icons, animations, and other features, enhancing the overall user experience on supported devices. The continued rollout of HyperOS 3.1 demonstrates Xiaomi's commitment to providing regular software updates to its users.

stories.headline: '007 First Light': Bond's origin story gets an explosive gaming debut From rugged Iceland to dangerous Mauritania and on to Antarctica: What sounds like a James Bond also is one - only one where you get to play 007 himself.
stories.summary: "007 First Light" is a new James Bond game where players take on the role of 007 himself. The game features an original story, with Bond's likeness not based on any of the film actors. It is set in various locations including Iceland, Mauritania, and Antarctica. The game offers a range of approaches to complete missions, including gadgets, fast cars, and non-violent spy techniques. With a 15.5-hour storyline, the game takes Bond to multiple countries, encountering intriguing characters and an overarching conspiracy. The game is available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, priced at $70, with a Nintendo Switch 2 version to follow in mid-2026. The game features excellent voice performances, including Patrick Gibson as Bond and Lennie James as Greenway.

stories.headline: Anthony Gordon is a Barcelona player! La Liga champions confirm €80m transfer after beating Bayern to Newcastle winger
stories.summary: Barcelona have confirmed the signing of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United in a deal worth €80million. The transfer includes a sell-on clause and sees the England winger join the La Liga champions. The announcement was delayed by four hours due to paperwork issues, with the club initially planning to reveal the signing at 1pm on Friday. However, the deal was finally confirmed late in the evening. Barcelona beat Bayern to secure Gordon's signature, with the 22-year-old becoming the latest addition to their squad. The transfer fee is equivalent to £69.3m or $93.2m, making it a significant investment for the club. Gordon's move to Barcelona marks a new chapter in his career, with the winger set to compete at the highest level in Spanish football.

stories.headline: Alphonso Davies in Canada World Cup squad despite injury
stories.summary: Canada's World Cup squad has been unveiled, with Alphonso Davies and Jonathan David as key players. Despite struggling with muscle injuries after an eight-month absence due to an ACL tear, Davies has been included in the 26-man roster. Canada, co-hosting the World Cup with the US and Mexico, aims to advance past the group stage for the first time. The team is in Group B alongside Switzerland, Qatar, and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Canada will play all three group-stage matches on home soil. This is Canada's third World Cup appearance, having previously participated in 1986 and 2022, where they finished at the bottom of their group. Davies scored Canada's first World Cup goal in 2022, and his inclusion in the squad is a significant boost to the team's chances. Coach Jesse Marsch has expressed confidence in his core group.

stories.headline: Cripps’ ‘out of body experience’ as ‘heroic’ skipper lifts lid on dramatic Blues turnaround
stories.summary: Carlton captain Patrick Cripps led his team to a dramatic turnaround, securing a 12.16 (88) to 12.12 (84) win over the Cats. Cripps came off the bench and took an epic contested mark at the top of the goal square, describing the moment as an "out-of-body experience." He finished with 30 disposals, eight clearances, and the match-winning goal in the dying minutes. The Blues held on despite the Cats' intense pressure in the final minute. Cripps' performance was instrumental in the team's victory, and he has been praised for his heroic efforts. The win is a significant turnaround for the Blues, who have been struggling in recent times. Cripps' leadership and skill were on full display, making him the difference-maker in the game.

stories.headline: Brewers pick up gritty 5-4 comeback win over Astros in 10 innings
stories.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers secured a 5-4 comeback win over the Houston Astros in 10 innings. The Brewers trailed by three runs before a two-run home run by Chourio in the fifth inning cut the lead to 4-3. In the 10th inning, a sacrifice fly by Turang lifted the Brewers past the Astros. Trevor Megill struck out two in the 10th to earn his seventh save. The Astros' new pitcher, Alimber Santa, made his major-league debut on Monday and pitched in the 10th inning. The Brewers' win marked a gritty comeback victory, overcoming an initial deficit to take the game in extra innings. The final score was 5-4 in favor of the Brewers, with Turang's sacrifice fly proving to be the decisive play.

stories.headline: Haryana suspends mobile internet in Faridabad's NIT Zone ahead of demolition drive Mobile data, bulk SMS and dongle services barred within 1-km radius amid fears of social media-fuelled unrest; voice calls and broadband services exempted.
stories.summary: Mobile internet services, including 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G, have been suspended in Faridabad's NIT Zone ahead of a demolition drive. The suspension, which also includes bulk SMS and dongle services, is in effect within a 1-kilometre radius of the area from 12:30 am to 10 pm on May 30. Authorities cited concerns over possible unrest and misinformation spread through social media as the reason for the suspension. Voice calls, banking SMS alerts, individual messages, broadband, and leased-line internet services remain exempt. The move aims to prevent the spread of rumours and inflammatory content that could lead to unrest. The order was issued on May 29 as a precautionary measure to maintain law and order in the area during the demolition drive scheduled for May 30.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Refuses To Review Judgment Mandating TET, Extends Deadline For In-Service Teachers "Service of teachers cannot come at the cost of educational future of the children," the Bench observed
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has refused to review a judgment mandating the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) for in-service teachers, stating that the service of teachers cannot compromise the educational future of children. The court emphasized that the TET requirement is linked to maintaining standards in elementary education and is a constitutional mandate for quality education. The bench directed states and authorities to conduct TET examinations periodically, preferably twice a year, and provide reasonable opportunities for in-service teachers to qualify. With this modification, all review petitions were dismissed, and the deadline for in-service teachers to clear the TET has been extended. The court aims to balance the interests of teachers with the need to ensure quality education for children. States and authorities are now required to conduct TET examinations regularly to maintain educational standards.

stories.headline: Exam fail: Indian students complain en masse about marking errors in key final exams New digital marking system is aimed at reducing human errors but many students say it has resulted in wrong grades
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) is facing criticism over its new On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for Class 12 board exams. The digital system, intended to reduce human errors, has resulted in alleged marking errors, with many students complaining about incorrect grades. Students have shared screenshots showing mismatched answer sheets and incorrect marking. The CBSE has acknowledged technical glitches and payment failures, and experts from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras have been sent to investigate. The issue has caused anxiety among students, with some reporting incorrect marks despite correct answers. The CBSE had extended the deadline for applications due to "unprecedented traffic" and "attempts of unauthorised interference" on the portal. Students are seeking re-evaluation and transparency in the marking process. The CBSE has emailed some students the "correct copy" of their answer sheets, but the issue remains unresolved.

stories.headline: Ex-IAS officer Dhanendra Kumar's 80th b’day, London trip, reunion plans gutted in fatal house blaze; how family tried to save him in vain
stories.summary: Ex-IAS officer Dhanendra Kumar's life was cut short in a fatal house blaze, just before his 80th birthday and a planned trip to London. The fire quickly spread, fueled by the false ceiling, and engulfed the furniture. Despite his family's best efforts to save him, they were unable to rescue Kumar. His family had been looking forward to celebrating his milestone birthday and a reunion. The plans, including the London trip, were all set to take place, but the tragic incident occurred, leaving the family in shock. The fire's rapid spread made it difficult for the family to save Kumar, and unfortunately, their efforts were in vain. The incident has resulted in the loss of a retired IAS officer, whose birthday and travel plans were eagerly anticipated by his loved ones.

stories.headline: BREAKING: Trump Set To Finalise Iran Nuclear Deal Tonight? Major Hormuz Strait Breakthrough Near
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is expected to make a final decision on a potential Iran agreement tonight. The proposed deal includes Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz without tolls and committing to never develop nuclear weapons. In return, Iran is seeking the lifting of sanctions. A tentative deal has been reached between the US and Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz and begin talks on Tehran's nuclear program, but Trump's approval is still required. Trump's demands include the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a commitment from Iran to never have nuclear weapons, and the removal of water mine bombs. A top adviser to Iran's supreme leader has stated that Iran is ready for a nuclear deal with Trump if sanctions are lifted.

stories.headline: US and Iran Reach Tentative Agreement on Nuclear Program and Sanctions Relief
stories.summary: US and Iranian negotiators have reached a tentative 60-day memorandum of understanding (MoU) to extend a fragile ceasefire and initiate formal talks on Iran's nuclear program. The agreement comes after sporadic skirmishes between the US and Iran in the Gulf, including limited attacks earlier on Thursday. The MoU aims to pave the way for discussions on Iran's nuclear program and potential sanctions relief. The tentative deal is significant, as it could lead to a reduction in tensions between the two countries. The 60-day ceasefire extension is intended to provide a window for substantive negotiations on the nuclear issue. The development is a notable diplomatic breakthrough, following a period of heightened tensions and skirmishes in the region. The talks on Iran's nuclear program are expected to commence, with the goal of reaching a more comprehensive agreement.

stories.headline: Iran Nuclear Deal: World Leaders React to Potential Breakthrough in Negotiations
stories.summary: US and Iranian negotiators have reached a tentative agreement to extend a ceasefire by 60 days and start new talks. The development comes after Iranian officials met in Doha for negotiations, which were preceded by US military strikes intended to protect troops. The US aims to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon, while Tehran denies such intentions. Recent comments from US officials suggest progress in peace efforts, but specific terms of a potential deal remain unclear. Tensions remain high following US and Israeli actions, with the US seeking a deal that addresses its concerns about Iran's nuclear program. The extension of the ceasefire and resumption of talks indicate a potential breakthrough in negotiations, with world leaders awaiting further developments and clarification on the terms of a possible agreement.

stories.headline: Hormuz Strait Tensions Ease as US and Iran Make Progress in Nuclear Talks
stories.summary: The US and Iran have made progress in nuclear talks, easing tensions in the Hormuz Strait. Iran has committed to reopening the Strait of Hormuz and disposing of its stockpile of enriched uranium. A tentative agreement has been reached to extend a fragile ceasefire by 60 days, reopen the strait, and establish a framework for broader talks on Tehran's nuclear program. The potential deal would also establish a framework for nuclear talks, ease sanctions on Iran, and unfreeze Tehran's overseas assets. A memorandum of understanding on a peace deal is largely negotiated, with both countries and mediators reporting progress. The agreement would include the disposal of highly enriched uranium, a key step towards resolving the conflict. The fragile ceasefire has been in place since April 8, with efforts underway to finalize the agreement.

stories.headline: MSCI index rejig, US-Iran deal worries spook Dalal Street Indian stock markets experienced a significant drop on Friday, with major indices closing lower
stories.summary: Indian stock markets experienced a significant drop on Friday, with major indices closing lower. The decline was largely driven by outflows related to the MSCI index rejig. Additionally, concerns over a potential US-Iran deal and its implications also contributed to the market downturn. The MSCI index changes led to a rebalancing of portfolios, resulting in outflows from the Indian market. Meanwhile, recent military actions and economic measures have weakened Iran's financial position, adding to the uncertainty. As a result, major stakeholders are looking to offload portions of their holdings, further impacting the market. The combined effect of these factors led to a significant drop in the Indian stock markets, with major indices closing lower on Friday. The market volatility is being closely watched by investors and analysts amid the ongoing geopolitical developments.

stories.headline: Stock Market Crash: What Is MSCI Rebalancing And Why Did It Trigger A Rs 5.7 Lakh Crore Sell-Off
stories.summary: Indian equity benchmarks fell sharply on Friday due to MSCI rebalancing, triggering a Rs 5.7 lakh crore sell-off. The exercise led to institutional selling, putting heavy pressure on heavyweight stocks. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 declined 1.30% and 0.85%, respectively. The sell-off was broad-based, with all sectors in the red, particularly IT, tech, auto, and telecom. MSCI rebalancing occurs periodically to adjust index constituents and weights, leading to large buy-sell orders that impact market prices. The May 2026 review resulted in Rs 8,000 crore net outflows from equities. The market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies was affected, standing at Rs 479 lakh crore on September 27, 2024, before the sell-off. The MSCI rebalancing triggered a sharp selloff in Indian stocks, causing significant market volatility.

stories.headline: MSCI Rebalancing Explained: The Global Index That Moved Indian Stocks In Minutes; Know Next Date
stories.summary: MSCI rebalancing occurred on May 29, 2026, causing a sharp selloff in Indian stocks during the final minutes of trading, pulling down benchmark indices BSE Sensex and NSE. MSCI, one of the world's most tracked stock market indices, reshuffles Indian stocks in its indices and adjusts their weight a few times a year. The rebalancing triggers significant passive fund flows across Indian equities, resulting in sharp market movements. The May 2026 MSCI Global Standard Index rebalancing is effective as of May 29. Trillions of dollars of global passive funds track MSCI indices, making its rebalancing a significant event for Indian stocks. The next rebalancing date is expected to be announced, which will again impact Indian equities. MSCI's periodic rebalancing is a key event for investors to watch, given its influence on global market trends.

stories.headline: Indian stock markets plunge as MSCI rebalancing leads to massive outflows
stories.summary: Indian stock markets experienced a significant plunge due to MSCI index rebalancing, resulting in massive outflows. The Sensex fell 1092 points and the Nifty slipped 359 points, with ₹5.77 trillion wiped out from Indian stocks in the last 30 minutes of trading. Foreign investors sold ₹21,106 crore worth of equities, marking record FII outflows. The MSCI index rebalancing triggered heavy institutional selling, leading to late-session selling pressure. Concerns over elevated crude oil prices and West Asia tensions also contributed to the market volatility. The benchmark indices witnessed a sharp sell-off, with the Indian stock markets tumbling due to the combined effects of MSCI rebalancing, foreign fund outflows, and global geopolitical tensions, indicating potential volatility ahead. The heavy selling pressure led to a substantial decline in the market value, affecting investor sentiment.

stories.headline: Ashok Leyland to establish Indonesia unit, deepen Pindad partnership
stories.summary: Ashok Leyland has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Indonesia's state-owned defence manufacturer PT Pindad to jointly develop and manufacture electric buses and defence vehicles. The partnership combines Ashok Leyland's expertise in commercial electric vehicle platforms and defence mobility solutions with PT Pindad's engineering capabilities and local manufacturing base. The collaboration aims to support sustainable mobility and modern defence needs in Indonesia. As part of its expansion, Ashok Leyland is establishing a unit in Indonesia and deepening its partnership with PT Pindad. The company is also setting up a new factory in Saudi Arabia and prioritizing its distribution footprint in the ASEAN region, while Europe and the UK remain lower on its priority list for now. This move marks a significant step in Ashok Leyland's global expansion, building on its existing presence in the GCC region.

stories.headline: Vertiv Holdings Stock: The AI Data Center Cooling Leader Still Has Momentum
stories.summary: Vertiv Holdings reported a standout quarter driven by a over 50% increase in its data center cooling solutions. The company provides critical digital infrastructure, power, cooling, and thermal management solutions for data centers. As a global leader in data center power management and thermal infrastructure, Vertiv is benefiting from strong AI infrastructure demand. In its fourth quarter, orders rose 252% and backlog more than doubled to about $15.0 billion. Vertiv's role in critical infrastructure for data centers and power systems has drawn attention to its potential. With a strong position in the market, Vertiv is well-placed to capitalize on the growing demand for AI infrastructure, driven by the need for efficient and reliable data center cooling solutions. The company's momentum is expected to continue into 2026.

stories.headline: Chasing billions: Indonesia’s commodity export crackdown sows confusion
stories.summary: Indonesia has introduced new export controls to curb deceptive trade practices, which have resulted in the loss of nearly $1 trillion in resource wealth over 34 years. President Prabowo Subianto announced the move, citing discrepancies between Indonesia's export declarations and actual import records in the US, with commodity prices at destination ports nearly double the reported domestic values. The new system will centralize exports of strategic commodities, including palm oil, under a 'single desk' model, where a state-owned enterprise will handle licensing, pricing, and clearance. This change may impact the global supply chain, sparking alarm in the industry. The move aims to prevent export proceeds from being retained offshore and to increase revenue for the Indonesian government. The new export controls are part of a broader effort to reform Indonesia's commodity export sector.

stories.headline: Nigerian Breweries appoints Runsewe as Human Resources Director
stories.summary: Nigerian Breweries Plc has appointed Nkechi Runsewe as its new Human Resources Director, effective August 1, 2026. She will succeed Grace Omo in the role. As Human Resources Director, Runsewe will play a key role in executing the company's EverGreen 2030 strategy by shaping its human resources initiatives. Nigerian Breweries Plc, Nigeria's leading brewing company, made the announcement, expressing pleasure at Runsewe's appointment. She is expected to bring her expertise to the position, driving the company's human resources efforts forward. The appointment is part of the company's efforts to achieve its strategic objectives, with Runsewe's leadership set to contribute to the company's continued success. Her appointment takes effect on August 1, 2026, marking a new chapter in the company's human resources management.
